learn.hook: A bicycle wheel touches the road at just ONE point — that road is a tangent to the wheel!
points: A secant is a line that meets a circle at two points. A tangent meets it at exactly one point, called the point of contact.
A circle has infinitely many tangents — one at every point on it.
From a point inside the circle there is no tangent, from a point on the circle exactly one, and from a point outside exactly two.
Theorem: the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
Tangents at the two ends of a diameter are parallel to each other.

example.q: A circle has radius 5 cm and a point P is 13 cm from its centre O. Find the length of the tangent from P.
steps: The radius OQ is perpendicular to the tangent PQ, so ΔOQP is right-angled at Q

learn.reallife: A car tyre touches the flat road at just one point, and a ruler laid against a bangle touches it at one point — the road and the ruler are tangents.

games.title: Tangent truths
items: A tangent meets a circle at exactly one point.
That single point is the point of contact.
A circle has exactly two tangents.
There is a tangent at every point, so infinitely many.
The tangent at a point is perpendicular to the radius through that point.
This is the main tangent theorem.
A secant meets a circle at two points.
It cuts right through the circle.
Tangents at the ends of a diameter are parallel.
Both are perpendicular to the same diameter.
Two tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it.
Every line through an inside point cuts the circle twice, so none is a tangent.

quiz.q: PQ is a tangent at Q to a circle with centre O. If OQ = 6 cm and OP = 10 cm, what is PQ?
quiz.mistake: Adds the squares instead of subtracting, or just subtracts 10 − 6

quiz.q: PQ touches a circle with centre O at Q, and ∠POQ = 60°. What is ∠OPQ?
quiz.explain: ∠OQP = 90° (tangent ⊥ radius). So ∠OPQ = 180° − 90° − 60° = 30°.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the angle between the tangent and the radius is 90°

quiz.q: How many tangents can a circle have?
quiz.explain: There is one tangent at every point of the circle, and a circle has infinitely many points.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only of the two tangents from one outside point

quiz.q: The tangent from P to a circle with centre O is 24 cm long and OP = 25 cm. What is the radius?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the lengths (25 − 24) without squaring

quiz.q: What is a line that meets a circle at two points called?
quiz.explain: A secant cuts the circle at two points, while a tangent only touches it at one.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the words secant and tangent

quiz.q: A circle has radius 3 cm. Two parallel tangents are drawn to it. How far apart are they?
quiz.explain: Parallel tangents touch the circle at the ends of a diameter, so they are a diameter apart: 2 × 3 = 6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the radius instead of the diameter

quiz.q: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it?
quiz.explain: Any line through an inside point crosses the circle at two points, so none of them is a tangent.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is always at least one tangent

quiz.q: A bicycle wheel rests on a flat road. What angle does the spoke from the hub to the touching point make with the road?
quiz.explain: The road is a tangent to the wheel, and the spoke is a radius to the point of contact, so they are perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the road to a tangent

teach.ask: Gappu rolls a bangle on the table: 'What is special about the table and the bangle's radius where they touch?'
teach.praise: Chirp! The tangent touches at one point, and the radius there makes a right angle with it!
teach.nudge: At how many points does a tangent touch, and what angle does it make with the radius?

learn.hook: From any point outside a circle, the two tangents you draw are always perfect twins — exactly the same length!
points: Theorem: the lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal: PA = PB.
Proof idea: ΔOAP and ΔOBP are right-angled at A and B, share the hypotenuse OP and have OA = OB, so they are congruent (RHS).
Tangent length from P: PA = √(OP² − r²).

example.q: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle with centre O, and ∠APB = 70°. Find ∠AOB and ∠OPA.

learn.reallife: A rope wrapped around a pulley from one fixed hook leaves the wheel along two equal tangent lengths.

games.title: Match the tangent fact
pairs: Two tangents PA and PB from P

quiz.q: PA and PB are tangents from P to a circle with centre O. If ∠APB = 80°, what is ∠AOB?
quiz.mistake: Thinks ∠AOB equals ∠APB

quiz.q: PA and PB are tangents with ∠APB = 80°. What is ∠AOP?
quiz.explain: OP bisects ∠APB, so ∠APO = 40°. In right ΔOAP, ∠AOP = 90° − 40° = 50°.
quiz.mistake: Gives ∠APO (40°) instead of ∠AOP

quiz.q: From P, the tangent PA to a circle is 12 cm long. How long is the other tangent PB?
quiz.explain: Tangents from an external point are equal, so PB = PA = 12 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more information is needed

quiz.q: PA and PB are tangents from P with ∠PAB = 65°. What is ∠APB?
quiz.explain: PA = PB, so ΔPAB is isosceles and ∠PBA = 65°. Then ∠APB = 180° − 130° = 50°.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the base angles of the isosceles triangle are equal

quiz.q: Two tangents from P to a circle of radius 5 cm are inclined at 60°. What is OP?
quiz.explain: ∠OPA = 30° and ∠OAP = 90°. sin 30° = OA/OP, so OP = 5 ÷ 1/2 = 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the full 60° instead of half of it

quiz.q: Tangents PA and PB from P make ∠APB = 60° with a circle of radius 5 cm. How long is PA?
quiz.explain: In right ΔOAP, ∠OPA = 30°, so tan 30° = OA/PA and PA = 5 ÷ (1/√3) = 5√3 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses tan 60° and gets 5/√3 cm

quiz.q: Why are the two tangents from an external point P equal?
options: Because all lines from P are equal
Because right triangles OAP and OBP are congruent by RHS
Because the angles at P are 90°
quiz.explain: OA = OB (radii), OP is common, and ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°. By RHS the triangles are congruent, so PA = PB.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason without using the right angles at A and B

quiz.q: Two tangents from P to a circle of radius 4 cm meet at 90°. What shape is OAPB?
options: A rhombus with no right angle
quiz.explain: ∠A = ∠B = ∠P = 90°, so ∠O = 90° too. OA = OB = 4 and PA = PB; a rectangle with two adjacent sides equal (OA = PA = 4 cm) is a square.
quiz.mistake: Notices equal tangents but not the four right angles

teach.ask: Gappu draws two tangents from his perch to a round pond: 'Are these two tangents the same length? Why?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Equal radii, right angles and a shared side make congruent triangles — so the tangents are twins!
teach.nudge: Which two triangles can I compare, and why are they congruent?

learn.hook: With the 'equal tangents' rule, puzzles about circles hiding inside triangles and squares become easy!
points: If a circle touches all four sides of quadrilateral ABCD, then AB + CD = AD + BC.
So a parallelogram that circumscribes a circle must be a rhombus.
In a triangle with an incircle, the two tangents from each vertex are equal, so each side splits into two known pieces.
For two concentric circles, a chord of the bigger circle that touches the smaller circle is bisected at the point of contact.
If TP and TQ are tangents from T, then ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.

example.q: A circle touches all four sides of ABCD. AB = 6 cm, BC = 7 cm and CD = 4 cm. Find AD.

learn.reallife: Designers of round ball-bearings packed inside square frames, or rangoli circles drawn inside squares, use these tangent rules.

games.title: Prove AB + CD = AD + BC
games.prompt: Circle touches AB, BC, CD, DA of quadrilateral ABCD
items: Let the circle touch AB, BC, CD and DA at P, Q, R and S
Tangents from one point are equal: AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, DR = DS
Add them: AP + BP + CR + DR = AS + BQ + CQ + DS
So AB + CD = AD + BC

quiz.q: Quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle, with AB = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm and CD = 7 cm. What is AD?
quiz.explain: AB + CD = AD + BC, so 8 + 7 = AD + 10 and AD = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Pairs adjacent sides instead of opposite sides

quiz.q: Two concentric circles have radii 13 cm and 5 cm. A chord of the larger circle touches the smaller one. How long is the chord?
quiz.explain: The radius 5 cm meets the chord at 90° at its midpoint. Half-chord = √(169 − 25) = 12, so the chord is 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to double the half-chord

quiz.q: The incircle of ΔABC touches AB at P, BC at Q and CA at R. AP = 4 cm, BQ = 6 cm and CR = 5 cm. What is the perimeter of ΔABC?
quiz.explain: Each tangent length appears twice: AP = AR, BP = BQ, CQ = CR. Perimeter = 2(4 + 6 + 5) = 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds each tangent length only once

quiz.q: A parallelogram circumscribes a circle. What kind of parallelogram must it be?
quiz.explain: AB + CD = AD + BC with AB = CD and AD = BC gives 2AB = 2BC, so all sides are equal: a rhombus.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any parallelogram can hold a circle touching all sides

quiz.q: In ΔABC, AB = 10 cm, BC = 8 cm and CA = 12 cm. Its incircle touches AB at P. What is AP?
quiz.explain: Let AP = AR = x. Then BP = BQ = 10 − x and CR = CQ = 12 − x. BQ + CQ = 8 gives 22 − 2x = 8, so x = 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the point of contact is the midpoint of AB

quiz.q: A rangoli circle is drawn inside a square frame of side 14 cm, touching all four sides. What is its radius?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides of the square are parallel tangents, so they are a diameter apart. Diameter = 14 cm, radius = 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Takes the side of the square as the radius

quiz.q: TP and TQ are tangents from T to a circle with centre O, and ∠PTQ = 70°. What is ∠OPQ?
quiz.explain: ΔTPQ is isosceles, so ∠TPQ = (180° − 70°)/2 = 55°. ∠OPT = 90°, so ∠OPQ = 90° − 55° = 35° (half of 70°).
quiz.mistake: Gives ∠TPQ (55°) instead of ∠OPQ

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the radius of its incircle?
quiz.explain: The hypotenuse is 10 cm. From the right-angle vertex both tangents equal r, so (6 − r) + (8 − r) = 10, giving r = 2 cm.
quiz.mistake: Halves a side instead of using tangent lengths

teach.ask: Gappu sees a circle snug inside a four-sided frame: 'Why do the opposite sides add up to the same total?'
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Equal tangents from each corner make the opposite sides add up the same. Neat!
teach.nudge: What do I know about the two tangents from each corner?
